text:
incident-bot: PAGER: Rapid GPU queue growth observed on prod-inference (nv-pool). Autoscaler failing to provision GPU nodes. Spike detected 18:03 UTC. Paging on-call. :rotating_light:
eli: I'll take this. Current backlog ~5k requests; 99th latency ~8s, errors up ~4%.
sam: confirmed. Multiple customers reporting retries. Which k8s cluster is affected?
eli: cluster=ml-prod-us-west2, target nodegroup=nv-gpu-1. ASG shows desired=0 max=4 but cluster-autoscaler logs: 'launch template mismatch' and repeated 'AttachRole not found' around scale attempts.
jin: Cloud logs show IAM failures: InstanceProfileAttachDenied and STS token errors around 17:58-18:02. Might be a transient permission cache issue or a rotated role.
elI: Proposed mitigations: 1) create temporary nodegroup with legacy launch template, 2) add tolerations on inference deployments, 3) raise cluster.maxNodes and disable aggressive scale-down. Any concerns?
lina: Fine. We'll prep a customer message before any cross-region routing.
infra-sre: Note autoscaler also hit cluster.maxNodes (40/40). We can raise it quickly but need cloud quota check for ASGs. If IAM attach fails, manual node creation will also fail unless we use a known-good instance profile.
eli: Running diagnostics: `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | egrep "Pending|CrashLoop"` ->
```
NAME                               READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE   NODE
model-serving-abc-5f7c8            0/1     Pending   0          3m   <none>
embedding-worker-22-dd9c           0/2     Pending   0          6m   <none>
prefetcher-7c8f9                   1/1     Running   0          15m  nv-gpu-2
```
eli: Events: `0/3 nodes are available: 3 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate.`
sam: So taint mismatch. Did the new launch template introduce a gpu-exclusive taint?
jin: Yes. lt-2026-03 has bootstrap adding `kubernetes.io/gpu=true:NoSchedule`. Older LTs didn't. Autoscaler attempted to create nodes with lt-2026-03 but pending instances don't satisfy existing pod tolerations, causing a scheduling gap until compatible nodes are available.
eli: Immediate actions: 1) manually create temporary ASG using legacy LT (nv-gpu-legacy), 2) patch deployments to tolerate the new taint to allow scheduling across both node types, 3) temporarily increase cluster.maxNodes to 60.
infra-sre: I'll create ASG manually but will override instance profile to gpu-role-v2 (known good). If attach role errors persist, we'll rely on manual profile attach.
lina: I'll draft a short customer status: "We're experiencing elevated inference latency due to GPU provisioning delays; mitigation in progress. No data loss; some requests may see 1-3 minute delays. Updates in 30m."
support-bot: Created customer ticket INC-8942 and linked to this incident.
eli: Executing ASG create: `aws autoscaling create-auto-scaling-group --auto-scaling-group-name nv-temp-4532 --launch-template LaunchTemplateId=lt-legacy --min-size=1 --max-size=4 --desired-capacity=2`
infra-sre: ASG created and instance profile gpu-role-v2 attached. Instances initializing; both reached InService and joined the cluster.
jin: One node had kubelet NotReady due to driver mismatch. Ran SSM driver install runbook; node is Ready now.
eli: After nodes Ready, patched deployments to add toleration: `kubectl patch deploy embedding -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"tolerations":[{"key":"kubernetes.io/gpu","operator":"Exists","effect":"NoSchedule"}]}}}}'` and same for model-serving.
sam: That should let pods schedule on both legacy and new LT nodes.
lina: Customer update posted: "Emergency GPU capacity added; queues draining. Expect residual latency for up to 15 minutes."
jin: Cloud provider notes indicate transient IAM policy cache caused some AttachRole failures; retries succeeded after ~5s in many cases. That likely explains flaky autoscaler behavior during the spike.
eli: Quick status: manual ASG added (2 nodes), deployments patched, GPU driver fix applied, cluster.maxNodes raised. Backlog dropped ~70% in 12 minutes.
sam: Follow-ups: 1) reconcile launch templates (align taint behavior), 2) remove temp ASG after stable, 3) run full postmortem.
infra-sre: I'll file infra ticket to revert the lt-2026-03 taint change and schedule a controlled rollout with canary nodes and validation. Also opening cloud quota request for higher ASG limits as preventative.
lina: Handoff: eli will monitor for 30m then hand off to jin at 19:00 UTC. I'll prepare a Sev-2 customer-impact summary for the postmortem.
eli: Note on-call handoff: Oncall-> jin at 19:00 UTC. Escalation criteria: backlog > 1k or error rate >5% -> escalate to eng-sre.
support-bot: Updated INC-8942: "Mitigation applied; queue draining. Monitoring ongoing."
jin: I'll remain on watch. Recommend alert: `autoscaler_attachrole_error_rate > 0.5%` to trigger earlier.
elI: Agree. Adding alert ticket and runbook to handle AttachRole transient failures. Retrospective items: include LT taint in rollout checklist, add autoscaler attach-role integration test, document manual ASG steps for oncall.
sam: Also add: verify cluster.maxNodes and cloud ASG quotas during maintenance windows.
lina: I'll draft the incident postmortem timeline and classify: "Sev-2 - partial service degradation ~23 minutes; required manual intervention."
incident-bot: Incident state -> Mitigation in progress; Monitoring. Handoff scheduled to jin at 19:00 UTC.
eli: Keeping dashboards open. Do not delete nv-temp ASG until backlog < 200. I'll post final update when stable.
sam: ack.
jin: ack, standing by.
